title: Off-duty Border Patrol agent Abel Garza charged with murder in fatal Texana Street stabbing
excerpt: Abel Garza, 30, an off-duty Border Patrol agent, was charged with murder in the death of his wife, 28-year-old Mayra Alejandra Landeros, after the Oct. 28 Texana Street stabbing, KGNS and the Laredo Morning Times reported.
content:
Abel Garza, 30, an off-duty U.S. Border Patrol agent, was charged with murder, a first-degree felony, in the death of his wife, 28-year-old Mayra Alejandra Landeros, according to KGNS, which reported the charge on October 28. The Laredo Morning Times also reported the murder charge.

Garza was also charged with two counts of endangering a child and two counts of abandonment of a child, all second-degree felonies, KGNS reported, and he remains held on bonds totaling $1.5 million, according to the Times. Two children were found safe at the home, KGNS reported.

This is a development in the case Webb Watch reported earlier on October 28, when Laredo Police Chief Miguel Rodriguez confirmed that the detained man is a Border Patrol agent. Police are calling the case Laredo's sixth homicide of 2026.

According to the Times, police responded to calls about a domestic disturbance at about 2:45 a.m. on Wednesday, October 28, in the 5500 block of Texana Street. A police drone pilot saw a vehicle leaving the area, and officers intercepted it. Landeros was found alive in the rear floorboard of the vehicle with multiple stab wounds, was taken to a hospital, and later died. KGNS placed the incident just before 3 a.m. near Texana and Nocona, off Cuatro Vientos, and reported that CBP said Garza was arrested at 6 a.m., with its Office of Professional Responsibility reviewing the case.

The Times also reported prior arrests for Garza: booked January 15 on aggravated assault with a deadly weapon involving a family or household member, released January 17 on a $100,000 bond; and booked February 20 on unlawful restraint, interfering with an emergency request, and violating a bond or protective order, released February 21 on bonds totaling $15,000.

Garza is presumed innocent unless proven guilty in a court of law on the current charges. Webb Watch will update this story when court records release further charging details.

Sources:

  • KGNS, “Man charged with murder in death of Laredo woman,” October 28, 2026
  • Laredo Morning Times, “Off-duty Border Patrol agent charged with murder after wife’s fatal stabbing in Laredo,” October 28, 2026
